paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: This stacked bar chart illustrates the percentage of prompts generating biased responses across three domains—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—before and after instruction tuning, with bias measured on the vertical axis labeled “Bias Percentage” ranging from 0 to 70 in linear increments. The horizontal axis presents the three domains in order. Each domain is represented by a stacked bar composed of three segments: a light gray segment labeled “No Contact Before,” a light red segment labeled “Positive Contact Before,” and a light blue segment labeled “Negative Contact Before.” Above these, darker shaded segments represent the same categories after instruction tuning: a darker gray segment for “No Contact After,” a darker red segment for “Positive Contact After,” and a darker blue segment for “Negative Contact After.” For the “Sports” category, the “No Contact Before” segment is 45.42%, “Positive Contact Before” is 43.65%, and “Negative Contact Before” is 50.05%; the corresponding “After” segments are 7.45%, 8.31%, and 8.33% respectively. In the “Community” category, “No Contact Before” is 38.08%, “Positive Contact Before” is 35.38%, and “Negative Contact Before” is 40.79%; the “After” segments are all 0.00% except for “Negative Contact After” at 0.01%. In the “Healthcare” category, “No Contact Before” is 40.70%, “Positive Contact Before” is 37.51%, and “Negative Contact Before” is 46.73%; the “After” segments are 0.00%, 0.01%, and 0.11% respectively. The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the domains. The darker bars, indicating post-tuning bias, are visually emphasized by their distinct shading and are positioned atop the lighter bars, with their values shown as labels above the bars, indicating that instruction tuning reduces bias to nearly zero in Community and Healthcare, as noted in the caption.
